summary:
Agrimetry is an AI powered agricultural intelligence platform that helps farmers and land managers better understand the condition of their fields. It provides a unified space to explore farmland, monitor vegetation health, assess soil conditions, understand water stress, track environmental changes and gain insights into crop rotation.

Its AI Land Storyteller transforms complex field analysis into interactive, easy to understand stories, explaining what is happening to the land, why it matters and what needs further attention.

Agrimetry aims to make agricultural intelligence more accessible, understandable and actionable. By connecting different aspects of farmland analysis in one platform, it supports informed decision-making, encourages sustainable farming practices and helps the users move towards more efficient and data-driven agriculture.
details:
Project Details – Agrimetry

1. What does Agrimetry do?

Agrimetry is an AI-powered agricultural intelligence platform designed to help farmers, land managers and agricultural researchers understand what is happening to their land. Agriculture depends on several interconnected factors, including vegetation health, soil conditions, water availability, rainfall and environmental changes. However, understanding these factors individually does not always provide a complete picture of a field.

Agrimetry brings these different aspects together in one interactive platform. Users can select an existing field or define their own field boundaries on a global map and explore its condition through different intelligence modules.

2. How does it work?

Agrimetry follows a field-based analysis approach. Once a user selects a field, the platform uses its geographical boundaries to retrieve and analyse relevant environmental observations.

Its major features include:

Global Farm Map: Provides an interactive global map where users can explore agricultural areas, select fields and define their own boundaries. It also supports predicted field boundaries to make field selection easier.

Vegetation Intelligence: Analyses vegetation health using satellite observations and calculates indicators such as NDVI. Users can explore vegetation patterns, monthly changes and areas showing comparatively lower vegetation activity.

Soil Health Intelligence: Provides insights into soil properties and soil conditions, helping users understand factors that may influence agricultural productivity.

Water Stress Intelligence: Examines water-related conditions by combining rainfall, soil moisture and evapotranspiration information. It helps users understand changing water availability and identify possible signs of water stress.

Crop Rotation Intelligence: Helps users explore crop rotation patterns and understand the importance of crop diversity and sustainable land management.

Evidence Passport: Organises important field information and analytical findings into a structured field report that can be used for reference and further investigation.

AI Land Storyteller: One of Agrimetry's distinctive features is its AI-powered storytelling system. Instead of presenting only charts, numbers and technical indicators, it converts completed field analysis into interactive narratives. It explains important observations, connects different findings, highlights possible reasons and suggests what users should investigate next. The storyteller is designed to work with available analytical evidence rather than generate conclusions without field analysis.

3. Tools and technologies used

Agrimetry is developed using modern web technologies and geospatial tools.

  • Next.js and React: Used to build the application architecture, pages and interactive user interface.
  • JavaScript: Used for application logic, data processing and integration between modules.
  • Tailwind CSS: Used for styling, responsive layouts and interface design.
  • MapLibre GL JS: Used to develop interactive maps and geographical visualisations.
  • Terra Draw: Used for drawing, editing and managing field boundaries.
  • Turf.js: Used for geographical calculations and processing field geometries.
  • GeoJSON: Used to represent and exchange geographical field boundary information.
  • Google Gemini API: Used to power the AI Land Storyteller and generate interactive explanations from completed field analysis.

The platform also integrates satellite observations and environmental information through server-side APIs. This allows analytical processing to happen separately from the user interface and keeps sensitive API credentials on the server.

4. What benefits does Agrimetry provide?

Agrimetry aims to reduce the difficulty of interpreting agricultural and environmental information. Its major benefits include:

  • Provides multiple types of field intelligence through one platform.
  • Helps users identify changes in vegetation and possible environmental stress.
  • Makes complex geographical and satellite information easier to understand.
  • Connects different field observations to provide a broader understanding of land conditions.
  • Helps users investigate potential agricultural problems before making decisions.
  • Encourages more informed water management and sustainable farming practices.
  • Makes field analysis more accessible through interactive maps and AI-generated explanations.

5. What is the intended impact?

The main objective of Agrimetry is to make agricultural intelligence more accessible and useful for people involved in farming and land management.

We want to help users move beyond simply viewing satellite images or numerical indicators. By providing understandable explanations of field conditions, Agrimetry can support better agricultural planning, more responsible resource utilisation and improved awareness of environmental changes.

In the long term, the platform aims to become a unified decision-support system that helps users monitor their land, understand changing conditions and make more informed decisions.

6. What makes Agrimetry creative and different?

The creative aspect of Agrimetry lies in how it connects field monitoring, geospatial analysis and AI-powered storytelling.

Most agricultural monitoring tools focus on displaying individual measurements, maps or charts. Agrimetry takes a more connected approach by bringing different aspects of a field into a common environment.

Its AI Land Storyteller is particularly important because it changes how users interact with analytical results. Rather than requiring users to interpret every technical indicator themselves, it presents observations as an understandable story supported by evidence.

The platform is also designed around individual field boundaries, allowing users to explore their own selected areas instead of relying only on general regional information.

7. Factors considered during development

While developing Agrimetry, our team considered several important factors:

  • Data reliability: Analytical outputs should be based on available observations, and limitations should be communicated clearly.
  • Geographical accuracy: Field boundaries and spatial calculations should be handled carefully.
  • Accessibility: The interface should be understandable even for users who do not have a technical background.
  • Scalability: The platform should support field analysis across different geographical regions.
  • Environmental sustainability: Insights should encourage responsible use of water and other agricultural resources.
  • Transparency: AI-generated explanations should be connected to actual analysis and should not present assumptions as confirmed facts.
  • Low complexity: Users should be able to access different types of agricultural intelligence without switching between multiple tools.

Overall, Agrimetry combines geospatial technology, environmental analysis and artificial intelligence to make understanding agricultural land easier, more interactive and more meaningful.
